comment:
* Utility class that you can call on with a timeout, and get called back * after a given time, dealing correctly with restarting the timeout. * *

For example, this class is used by the android.os.Vibrator class.

variables.name: mOffAt
variables.comment: turn it off at this time.

methods.name: public abstract void on(boolean alreadyOn)
methods.comment:
* Override this do what you need to do when it's starting
     * This is called with the monitor on this method held, so be careful.
     *
     * @param alreadyOn is true if it's currently running

methods.name: public abstract void off()
methods.comment:
* Override this to do what you need to do when it's stopping.
     * This is called with the monitor on this method held, so be careful.

methods.name: public void go(long milliseconds)
methods.comment:
* Does the following steps. *

1. Call on()

*

2. Start the timer.

*

3. At the timeout, calls off()

*

If you call this again, the timeout is reset to the new one

methods.name: public void cancel()
methods.comment: * Cancel the timeout and call off now.
